messages:
incident-bot: Pager: P0 - GPU node provisioning failing for gpu-pool-prod; queue growth detected (>900 pending pods). Autoscaler alerting: 5 scale attempts failed in 12m. Instance attach errors: AttachInstanceProfileFailed.

maya (on-call): I'm taking it. first triage: is this ASG/LaunchTemplate or IAM?

sam (sre): Logs from cluster-autoscaler show repeated failures: "could not create node: launch template version mismatch" then IAM errors when attaching instance profile. stacktrace attached to the alert.

kai (infra): Checking cloud console — the gpu-asg has reached desired=max (10) and account instance-profile attach rate-limited by control-plane (AWS API 429 spikes). Also seeing a new launch-template version rolled out yesterday with a different instance profile name (gpu-role-v2) but nodegroup expects gpu-role.

lin (support): Customer impact: multiple customer requests are getting 429s and backoff in our request queue; per-route numbers: text-gen-high latency/429s ~ 18% over last 10m, embeddings queue doubled. Affected customers: two mid-market customers on Dedicated with strict SLAs — I opened support tickets.

maya (on-call): Good context. Short-term mitigation plan: 1) reduce incoming concurrency to the queued routes, 2) flip fallback to CPU-optimized model for non-latency-critical traffic, 3) manual node add or bump ASG/max to allow capacity while infra fixes template/iam. Thoughts? :raising_hand:

sam (sre): Agreed. I can patch the autoscaler to allow joining instances with the new launch-template by adding an annotation and rolling CA. But that takes ~10m. Recommend manual ASG increase + manual instance launch with the old instance profile name to keep things predictable.

kai (infra): I can manually launch 2 GPU instances with the expected user-data/launch template reference and attach the correct instance profile to match kube labels. Doing manual launches now. If we bump ASG max make sure we have quota in the account. Also we should roll back the LT or update nodegroup config — I'd prefer updating LT to include the old profile alias to avoid more breaks.

maya (on-call): lin — can you throttle incoming routes? provide the exact command we use in gateway to reduce concurrency?

lin (support): On gateway: set route concurrency limit. Example: 
```
POST /admin/route-config
{ "route": "text-gen-high", "concurrency": 16 }
```
I'm applying to affected routes now.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started: fallback-cpu-model v2 -> 10% traffic for text-gen-high at 2025-10-02T14:15Z

maya (on-call): sam — can you post the autoscaler patch commands if someone needs to roll it?

sam (sre): Yeah. Patch (kubeconfig cluster-prod): 
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment cluster-autoscaler --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"ca-temporary-allow":"true"}}}}}'
# then restart pods:
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment cluster-autoscaler
```
Caveat: will allow new LT to join but we still need the correct instance profile or nodes will fail kube bootstrap.

kai (infra): Manual launches done: 2 x p4d-ish (labels match). They show NotReady until kubelet finished but then they Joined. ASG bump requested: increased desired=12, max=14 temporarily. Cloud console reports attach API throttling reduced after spreading launches.

lin (support): Traffic throttle + CPU fallback live. early signal: queue length dropping from 900 -> 420 in 8m, 429 rate down to 6%. Not fully recovered yet.

maya (on-call): Good. Customer comms: lin, please post interim notice to the two affected customers that we have partial mitigation, degraded throughput, and ETA for full recovery ~1h while infra finishes launch-template fix. Use template: 
"We're seeing provision delays for GPU-backed inference; we've applied routing controls and temporary CPU fallback. Throughput reduced but stable. Engineering is performing mitigations; we'll update in 30m."

ops-lead: Also capture who changed launch template yesterday — tagging infra release owners. We'll need a timeline in the postmortem.

sam (sre): I'm running a reconcile to update nodegroup launch template reference to gpu-role-v2 with a backwards-compatible alias, and adding a small retry/backoff on instance-profile attach in our boot script. Will push a hotfix in 20m.

kai (infra): Patch applied to LT to map gpu-role and gpu-role-v2 via new IAM alias; ASG now successfully launches additional instances. Watch for taints: one node came up with unexpected taint: node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable=true due to kubeadm drift — I'm cleansing it now: 
```
kubectl get nodes | grep gpu | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -n1 kubectl taint nodes --all node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable- || true
```

maya (on-call): What's ETA for full RTO?

lin (support): Current projection: if queues keep dropping at current rate, throughput back to normal in ~35-50m. I'll update customers in 30m.

deploy-bot: fallback-cpu-model v2 -> 50% traffic ramp at 2025-10-02T14:35Z (automated)

sam (sre): Hotfix pushed. Autoscaler now accepts both LT names; added 3s exponential backoff in instance profile attach. Autoscaler pods restarted at 14:28Z.

kai (infra): Verified 4 additional GPU nodes now in Ready state, no taints. ASG usage back under control. No more attach 429s in logs.

maya (on-call): Great. I'm going to monitor for 1h and then handoff to night on-call. Please add any followups to the incident tracker. Before handoff: lin confirm customer notices posted?

lin (support): Posted initial notices and updated tickets. Will send final follow-up after 30m.

ops-lead: Please schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 PT. Add action items: stricter LT rollout checks, autoscaler LT compatibility tests, and alert thresholds for launch-template drift.

maya (on-call): Handoff note: mitigations applied (gateway throttle, CPU fallback, manual node add, LT hotfix). System stable, RTO met. Handoff to night on-call @sam on duty at 18:00 PT.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to monitoring state by maya (on-call).
